newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BONDS IDLE LOW, DRACHMA UP VS MARK, DOWN VS $.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BONDS IDLE LOW, DRACHMA UP VS MARK, DOWN VS $.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards were sitting tight, holding morning levels and bonds were trading around intra-day lows in late calm trade, dealers said.
The drachma continued to gain ground against the soft mark but retreated against the robust dollar and was stable vis-a-vis the ecu, traders said.

"Depos and forex forwards are little changed and volume is thin," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "It is surprising to me that short-term rates including spotnext trade low, around 10 percent, with an bond auction in sight."
Bonds were steady after being battered in early trade with yields stabilising around intra-day highs, dealers said.
"Bonds are hovering around intra-day lows," said a senior bond dealer at a private bank. "I think we are in a downward channel."

Other dealers said the drop in bond prices should be expected with a number of banks raising money for the bond auction on July 15 and the central bank's fixed rate depo tender for 14-day funds on Wednesday.

"It is not a secret that a number of players seek to raise money for the bond auction and the central bank's 11.90 percent depo tender of 14-day funds on Wednesday," said a bond dealer at a foreign bank. "Foreign demand for bonds is weak and somebody has to fill the gap."
The yield on the 10-year coupon bond was little changed around 9.40 percent.

Greece will seek bids for a further 75 billion drachmas each of five- and seven-year bonds with coupons of 9.2 percent and 8.9 percent respectively, and 120 billion drachmas of 8.8 percent, 10-year bonds on July 15, the finance ministry announced late on Thursday.
The five- and seven-year bonds were auctioned for the first time ever on March 19 and then bids were re-opened on June 17. The 10-year bonds were auctioned for the first time ever on June 17.
Greece will also auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year floating rate notes on July 29.
The mark was quoted at 156.75/80 from Monday's 156.780 fix, the dollar at 280.83/93 drachmas from 281.270 and the ecu at 309.53/63 from 309.52 drachmas.

"Ecu/drachma has been fluctuating in the tight 309.45/70 range all day and volume has been thin," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "The drachma gained against the mark in line with the latter's weakness against EMS currencies breaking the 157 level on the downside."
The dollar continued to show strength against the drachma, piercing the 280 resistance, dealers said.
"Movements in dollar/drachma reflect the U.S. currency's strength against the mark and other currencies in world markets," said a forex dealer.
